title: FIG. 03 · Strata, closed
summary: Your round-2 strata assembly is back, grown up to three layers. The slabs drop in and close up into one stack, the red walks down them, and then one line carries what Intelligence learns back up into Narrative, so the closed loop reads at a glance.
story: Straight after the letter's "every quarter starts from zero", this section shows what Kelwin installs instead: three named layers, plus the one line that keeps what each quarter learned. It hands the principle a system that now gives off one clear signal ("In a noisy market, the clearest company wins").
motion: Standalone: the heading rises in like every other section. Then the three slabs drop in spread apart, top to bottom, with Narrative already red. Each one draws its own mark: lines of text, a route, a ring. The stack closes up while the measurement beside it changes from "3 layers" to "1 system". The red steps down to 02, then 03. The one return line then draws from the bottom slab back up into the top one, and the red lands back on 01. It takes about 5.8 seconds, plays once, and nothing loops afterwards.
On the homepage: the same sequence plays once, when the drawing itself is about half in view, so it isn't missed below the fold. There is no pin, and the page scrolls normally.

Interaction: every row in the list is a button. Pressing one finishes the drawing at once and moves the red, with a slight lift, to that layer. The link under the list stays in place while rows open and close.
Reduced motion: the finished drawing shows straight away (installed, loop drawn, 01 open), with no timers.
addressed: "I really liked the round 2 strata assembly … where it animates": that is now the section's whole design language. It has the same flat slabs, the boxed numbers on the right, the "1 system" measurement, the corner marks, the title block and the list beside the drawing. The slabs still drop in and close up into one stack, and the red still marks the layer you are reading.

"Too cluttered": the section is one drawing and one list, and nothing else. Gone are the four loop labels, the error stamp, the counter, the running dots, the scroll-locked frames and the five-step progress bar.

"Too hard to understand. Nothing seems clear": there are three layers, each named in plain words on the drawing and in the list with its one-line job. A revenue leader can say what gets installed, layer by layer, in a few seconds.

The closed loop now costs almost no ink. A single line runs from the bottom layer back into the top one, with one quiet label: "Feeds back what works". On entrance the red walks down 01 → 02 → 03 and that line carries it back to 01, so the motion shows the loop once and then rests.

The heading stays "Three layers. One closed loop." The line from your About page about the loop most teams run ("Capital in, campaigns run, knowledge lost, reset …") now sits beside it as a quiet note. The contrast is told in words instead of drawn as a second diagram.
notes: COPY SOURCES. Statement ★ 'Three layers. / One closed loop.' (architecture X, kept). Lede: stack X's 'Four layers Kelwin installs in your company, so pipeline becomes a standing output, not a one-time deliverable.', recast as 'Kelwin installs all three in your company, so pipeline becomes a standing output, not a one-time deliverable.' REPORTED DEVIATION: the /about caption (★ in STORY §2) did not fit cleanly as the lede. Without the drawn broken loop, 'The loop conserves nothing' straight under 'One closed loop.' reads as if it describes Kelwin's own loop. It is kept verbatim but moved to the head's note slot, under the label 'The loop most teams run' (system S's frame-0 name), so the ★ handoff from the letter is still rendered. Return label 'Feeds back what works' is from architecture X's approved lede ('Intelligence feeds back what works'). It was chosen over 'The return', which a revenue reader can take for ROI. Ledger: nav names and descriptors (D2). 'What it is' for 01 and 03 is from stack X; 03's 'narrative and channels' became 'narrative and infrastructure' to match the three-layer names. 02's line is trimmed from capability-data's GTM Infrastructure overview: deliverability and sequencing were dropped to stay out of Plurel's distribution lane. 'In practice' comes from stack X (01, 03) and system S (02). The tail 'If we’re not the fix, the audit says so — and points you somewhere better.' is from system S. The quiet door 'Find your weakest layer →' goes to /audit. There are no new numbers, years, clients or results, and the drawing's title block reads Specimen. The retired slogan is not used (D5). GEOMETRY (generated in face coordinates, as in stack X): three rectangular slabs at 184×120 units, 14px thick, true 30° iso. Pitch is 132 installed and 176 exploded. Every inscription sits in the visible part of its face, even with the 8px lift. One inscription each: text rules (Narrative), one input routed through a hub to three outputs (Infrastructure), and an open ring with a node at its gap (Intelligence). The return is one orthogonal 1px paper line, slab 03 left corner → out 40px → up → into slab 01 left corner, with one up-chevron and one inbound chevron. Its arms meet each slab's corner edge 4px below the corner, so they still touch when a slab lifts. The '3 layers → 1 system' dimension now sits after the callout names, as a brace over the three named layers. The left side carries the return, and a dimension there would collide with it. QUOTAS: 1 drawing; 3 callouts; 1 dimension; 4 registration marks; 1 title block of 4 cells (Fig. 03 · Revenue OS · Exploded→Installed · Specimen). RED MAP: label square, rule, the note's label square (as stack X), and the selected slab's top face. The return is paper, not red. LIVE BEHAVIOUR: the head runs on the kit's .is-play. The figure and ledger entrance is keyed to .is-go, which the script adds when the figure is 45% in view under html.km-home (at once in the standalone). Until then the figure is held hidden by .is-armed, which only the script adds, so with no script the drawing simply shows at rest. No pin and no ScrollTrigger. The detail column stretches to the sheet's height and its door is pushed to the bottom, so the door shares the title block's baseline and never moves while rows open; the tallest open row still fits. ≤760px: the ledger follows the drawing. The drawing scales to the column (the script sets --fs). Callouts, the dimension and the registration marks are visibility-hidden (the numbered ledger is the key), and the statement is 44px and full width. Use visibility, not display:none: the screenshot harness briefly matches the ≤760px query during full-page captures, and display:none restarts the fade animations, so those elements went missing in the shots. PRODUCTION: the exploded/installed and selection states are plain class toggles with CSS transitions, so they port directly to Motion. The same sequence timings apply (drop 700ms, 140ms stagger; close-up at 2.2s; steps at 3.05s and 3.85s; return 4.5–5.5s; red back on 01 at 5.35s).
